messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED PAGE: host gpu-az3-node-117 is UNREACHABLE (no heartbeat). Pager: PagerDuty auto page to #eng-oncall.
pagerduty: Page created (high) — triggered by monitor host-heartbeat-check. Incident key: PD-INC-8675309. Escalation timer started.
sam.oncall: ack — I'll take first look. pinging console and IPMI now.
emily.infra: on it. ssh/tcp to node times out, IPMI web is 503 and console shows login prompt flicker then blank.
raj.platform: from controlplane logs: kubelet last heartbeat 00:04:32 ago, Node condition Ready=false, reason=KernelOops in last event. pushing last kubelet logs: 
```
Mar 12 02:10:11 kubelet[123]: evicted: kernel: [E] KernelOops: GPU driver Xid 79...
Mar 12 02:10:12 kubelet[123]: runtime: kubelet started backoff loop
Mar 12 02:12:45 heartbeater: failed to ping host
```
(might be truncated)
mika.night: :eyes: starting evacuation plan: cordon + drain. will shift critical pods to standby nodes. any PVs using local NVMe?
ops-sre: checklist: 1) cordon node, 2) drain non-daemonset pods, 3) mark volumes read-only if local, 4) open RMA if hardware fault.
sam.oncall: running: `kubectl cordon gpu-az3-node-117 && kubectl drain gpu-az3-node-117 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
emily.infra: I see NVMe SMART errors in IPMI logs, could be NVMe power glitch. opening ticket with hwops now: RMA-37921. putting hardware into quarantine.
pagerduty: Page escalated to L2 after 5m (no L1 ack). Notified: @raj.platform, @emily.infra (oncall).
raj.platform: rolling out failover for the model-serving pool: re-routing new requests to gpu-az2 and gpu-az1 via traffic manager. Expected capacity drop ~20% for a few minutes.
mika.night: drain in progress: 27/31 pods evicted, blocked 4 pods due to local PVCs. tagging them for manual migration.
sam.oncall: customer impact: initial spike in errors from /v1/generate for customers using us-east-1 dedicated — observed 502s for ~8 min, estimated affected customers: 3 high-volume tenants (IDs redacted). posting note to incident channel soon.
ops-sre: temporary mitigation applied: traffic manager fallback policy engaged to use lower-latency replicas in us-east-2. Watch for increased token latency.
emily.infra: hwops confirmed PSU rail dropout event correlating with host timestamps. suspect surge caused GPU driver fault. RMA scheduled, replacement tomorrow in tech window.
raj.platform: health checks green on failover pools, error rate dropped to baseline ~3m after reroute. continuing to monitor for edge cases.
mika.night: handing off to night shift oncall @mika.night — I’ll be primary until 08:00 UTC. leaving cordon in place.
sam.oncall: thanks — I created followup tickets: INFRA-4421 (RMA & replacement), KUBE-1289 (investigate kubelet crash loop & kernel oops), and OPS-5002 (postmortem prep).
ops-sre: suggested next steps in runbook: run `nvme list` on replacement, validate kernel/drivers, apply kernel flags workaround if seen again, and create alert to correlate PSU flaps across rack.
emily.infra: snapshot of node logs uploaded to storage: s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-INC-8675309/gpu-az3-node-117.tar.gz
raj.platform: monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood/mon/dashboards/node-heartbeat?node=gpu-az3-node-117
mika.night: final note before sleep: node remains cordoned, workloads stable on fallback nodes, customer impact resolved. I'll kick off postmortem draft in the morning. :white_check_mark:
sam.oncall: handoff acked. tagging postmortem owner @ops-sre. closing pager for now; will reopen if regression.
